mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the current month reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same period are not statistically lower than during the previous 60-day period (p > 0.05), or the Fed reverses rate hikes within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 5% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when both PAYEMS momentum and UNRATE decline are present.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% suggests expanding economic activity, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite INDPRO showing upward momentum for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 105 suggests softening demand and deflationary pressure, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when both INDPRO and CPIAUCSL are below 105.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 5%, it indicates a shift toward accommodative policy, which typically increases risk appetite and yields a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the 3-month FEDFUNDS decline period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market, which can fuel wage growth and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% in a month while UNRATE remains flat or falls
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when PAYEMS spikes without UNRATE increase.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) below 102 accompanied by stable industrial production (INDPRO) suggest deflationary pressure without weakening supply, which can erode equity valuations and produce negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 102 for 3 consecutive months AND INDPRO > 110 for the same period
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative (p > 0.05) during the deflationary window.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a high-unemployment, low-inflation environment (UNRATE > 6% and CPIAUCSL < 105) weakens consumer and business sentiment, typically resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: regime condition: UNRATE > 6% AND CPIAUCSL < 105 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative (p > 0.05) during the identified regime.
